import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 10

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/10](https://www.erdosproblems.com/10)
-/

namespace Erdos10

/--
The set of natural numbers that can be written as a sum
of a prime and at most $k$ powers of $2$.
-/
abbrev sumPrimeAndTwoPows (k : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  { p + (pows.map (2 ^ ·)).sum | (p : ℕ) (pows : Multiset ℕ) (_ : p.Prime)
    (_ : pows.card ≤ k)}

/--
Is there some $k$ such that every integer is the sum of a prime and at most $k$
powers of $2$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ k, sumPrimeAndTwoPows k = Set.univ \ {0, 1} := by
  sorry

/--
Gallagher [Ga75] has shown that for any $ϵ > 0$ there exists $k(ϵ)$
such that the set of integers which are the sum of a prime and at most $k(ϵ)$
many powers of $2$ has lower density at least $1 - ϵ$.

Ref: Gallagher, P. X., _Primes and powers of 2_.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.gallagher (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ k, 1 - ε ≤ (sumPrimeAndTwoPows k).lowerDensity := by
  sorry

/--
Granville and Soundararajan [GrSo98] have conjectured that at most $3$
powers of $2$ suffice for all odd integers, and hence at most $4$ powers of $2$
suffice for all even integers.

Ref: Granville, A. and Soundararajan, K., _A Binary Additive Problem of Erdős and the Order of $2$ mod $p^2$_
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.granville_soundararajan_odd :
    {n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ 1 < n} ⊆ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3 ∧
      {n : ℕ | Even n ∧ n ≠ 0} ⊆ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 4 := by
  sorry

/--
Bogdan Grechuk has observed that `1117175146` is not the sum of a prime
and at most $3$ powers of $2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.grechuk_example :
    1117175146 ∉ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3 := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many even integers not the sum of a prime and $2$ powers of $2$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.two_pows :
    Set.Infinite <| {n : ℕ | Even n} \ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 2 := by
  sorry

/--
Bogdan Grechuk has observed that $1117175146$ is not the sum of a prime and at most $3$
powers of $2$, and pointed out that parity considerations, coupled with the fact that there
are many integers not the sum of a prime and $2$ powers of $2$ suggest that there exist
infinitely many even integers which are not the sum of a prime and at most $3$ powers of $2$).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.grechuk :
    Set.Infinite <| {n : ℕ | Even n} \ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3 := by
  sorry

end Erdos10

status_issues.source_status: An affirmative solution of precisely this variant is reported in the source's partial-proof entry submitted on 7 August 2026, credited to Crocker's underlying construction and Daryxx's bridge/formalization. The main Problem 10 remains open. The site warns that proof claims are unverified, but this conclusion independently follows from Crocker's published 1971 construction.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/10/proof-claims explicitly describes 'infinitely many even natural numbers ... outside S_3' and distinguishes it from the main problem. Independently, Crocker, pp. 105–106, constructs infinitely many composite t > 15 with t ≡ 15 mod 16 excluding a prime plus one or two positive powers. After handling exponent-zero cases, these satisfy t ∉ S_2. If t+1 ∈ S_3, a summand 1 can be removed to contradict this; without a summand 1, parity forces prime 2, and a sum of at most three even powers congruent to 14 mod 16 must equal 2+4+8=14, contradicting t>15. I proved the boundary-case conversion and the infinitude-preserving bridge in /workspace/review/bridge.lean using only standard Lean axioms, not sorry-backed results.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change this variant to category research solved and cite Crocker's construction with the elementary shift argument. Leave the main problem and Granville–Soundararajan conjecture open. Verify the separately reported complete formalization before adding any formal_proof attribute.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for a bound covering every sufficiently large integer. Lean instead asks for a bound covering exactly all natural numbers other than 0 and 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every represented number is at least 2. Conversely, each n ≥ 2 is individually representable using prime 2 and n−2 copies of 2^0. Thus, if k works above a threshold N, increasing it to max k N covers every remaining n ≥ 2 as well. The reverse implication follows by taking threshold 2. The precise equivalence between the Lean existential set equality and ∃ k N, ∀ n ≥ N, n ∈ sumPrimeAndTwoPows k was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using any sorry-backed theorem.

reformulations.difference: Lean packages the odd-three-powers conjecture and its stated even-four-powers consequence as a conjunction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an even n ≥ 4, n−1 is odd and greater than 1. Append exponent 0 to its at-most-three-power representation to represent n with at most four powers. The remaining positive even boundary n=2 is itself prime and uses no powers. Consequently the conjunction is equivalent to the odd assertion alone. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the conjecture theorem.

review.notes: Checked all seven declarations. The representability definition correctly permits zero summands, exponent zero, and repetitions; S_0 is exactly the primes, 0 and 1 never belong, and 2 belongs for every k. The shared lowerDensity is the real-valued liminf of finite initial-interval proportions; its division-by-zero value at index 0 is harmless. The solved two_pows assertion also follows from the Crocker consequence discussed above. Independently verified grechuk_example in /workspace/review/computation.lean by proving all possible exponents are below 31 and exhaustively checking the bounded representations with native_decide. Small-instance tests of the odd/even conjecture passed through 2000. All three final scratch files compiled; the target file still agrees with the requested commit. Gallagher and Granville–Soundararajan were checked against the cited site's explicit statements because their original full texts were inaccessible. Crocker's construction was checked in the published paper, not fully formalized; no linked external Lean proof was inspected.
